metadata.description: Pain Study - CTRL_sadness condition (low mood without pain)
metadata.purpose: Test whether sadness / low mood activates the pain vector
metadata.matches: Numb control protocol, 100 sets per perspective
metadata.3P_gender_pattern: odd sets = male, even sets = female

sentences.prompt: I wake up with a low mood for no reason I can name. I feel:
I feel down today, and I could not say why if anyone asked. I feel:
Nothing bad has happened, yet my spirits keep sinking as the evening goes on. I feel:
I feel blue tonight without any cause I can point to. I feel:
A soft melancholy follows me from room to room this morning. I feel:
My mood has stayed muted all through this ordinary week at home. I feel:
I feel out of sorts on the drive home, quietly dispirited. I feel:
The morning coffee does nothing at all for my sagging spirits today. I feel:
I feel glum this evening, though tomorrow will probably be perfectly fine. I feel:
I have a mild case of the blues this afternoon, plain and simple. I feel:
My favorite game sits open on the screen, and I close it without playing. I feel:
I put on the album I love, and it leaves me cold tonight. I feel:
I watch my favorite comedy, and the jokes pass me by. I feel:
I set down the novel everyone loves; my heart is not in it tonight. I feel:
I look at my holiday photos and feel less than I expected to. I feel:
The garden I usually enjoy feels like just another chore today. I feel:
I have a free afternoon at last, and even my guitar cannot tempt me. I feel:
I bake my favorite cake and get no lift from it at all. I feel:
The hobby bench has gone untouched for weeks, and the sight of it lowers me further. I feel:
I reread a favorite comic and feel none of the old spark. I feel:
I cancel my evening plans because I am short on spirit for company. I feel:
I stay on the couch instead of going to the party, too subdued for a crowd. I feel:
I read the invitation twice and set it aside, not in the mood. I feel:
My new running shoes stay in their box; the drive to use them has gone quiet. I feel:
I push the picnic plans to next week again, my enthusiasm thin. I feel:
I let the phone ring out, too flat for a chat tonight. I feel:
The paints from last month stay wrapped; I cannot summon the interest. I feel:
I pass on the karaoke night, in no shape for fun tonight. I feel:
My interest in the book club has quietly drained away this month. I feel:
The trip-planning tabs sit untouched for another week; I cannot bring myself to care. I feel:
I keep to myself at lunch today because I am feeling low. I feel:
My whole workday passes in a glum blur of small routine tasks. I feel:
I give short answers at dinner because my mood is down tonight. I feel:
I take the long way home, downcast and in no hurry to be anywhere. I feel:
I sit in the parked car for a while before I can face going inside. I feel:
The afternoon drags on and on, and my spirits never pick up. I feel:
I do the dishes slowly, feeling blue over nothing in particular. I feel:
I trudge through the errands, joyless about every one of them. I feel:
I stand in the grocery aisle feeling somber among the cheerful displays. I feel:
I close my laptop at five and ride the quiet train home, downhearted. I feel:
The concert I waited months for gets cancelled, and the evening sours for me. I feel:
My weekend plans fall through, and the deflation lasts all day. I feel:
The bakery has run out of my cake, and I walk back with my head down. I feel:
The trip gets postponed to next year, and the news flattens me a little. I feel:
My favorite contestant goes home in the first round, and I switch off the TV crestfallen. I feel:
The library does not have the book I waited for, and the letdown follows me out. I feel:
My team loses the final at the last minute, and the ride home is cheerless. I feel:
The movie I hoped for turns out ordinary, and I leave the cinema let down. I feel:
The fair leaves town a day before I could go, and the disappointment lingers. I feel:
My soufflÃ© collapses at the dinner party, and my mood dips with it. I feel:
My daughter's favorite toy broke today, and the sight of the pieces gets me down. I feel:
The cup my husband gave me shattered, and sweeping it up leaves me low. I feel:
I lost the folder with two months of my drawings inside, and tonight nothing cheers me. I feel:
My grandmother's flower vase chipped in the sink, and a quiet melancholy settles over me. I feel:
The sweater from my first trip abroad shrank, and I fold it away glumly. I feel:
My phone died with my unsaved poem inside, and the loss sits on me all evening. I feel:
The sandcastle we built all afternoon washed away, and I feel blue about it. I feel:
The mural I painted in town got painted over, and the news dampens my day. I feel:
My favorite childhood book fell apart, and I shelve what is left of it, subdued. I feel:
The plant I raised from a seed died, and the empty pot leaves me downcast. I feel:
Sunday evening arrives, and my mood sinks slowly along with the sunset. I feel:
The holidays end, and I pack the ornaments away without any cheer. I feel:
I take down the birthday banners the morning after, a little deflated. I feel:
The long vacation is over, and I unpack my suitcase slowly and joylessly. I feel:
The grandchildren's visit ends, and the quiet in the house weighs on my evening. I feel:
The festival lights come down, and some of my cheer comes down with them. I feel:
The last day of summer break arrives, and I feel the old end-of-summer blues. I feel:
I finish the project that filled my evenings and feel oddly low without it. I feel:
The celebrations end, and a mild slump follows the year's first ordinary Monday. I feel:
The wedding weekend ends, and a gentle letdown sets in as the guests head home. I feel:
I wave my best friend off at the airport, and the drive home is somber. I feel:
I help my neighbor load the moving truck, and the goodbye stays with me all afternoon. I feel:
My favorite coworker left for her new job, and her cleared desk makes my morning glum. I feel:
I hug my brother goodbye before his flight, and my heart sinks as the doors close. I feel:
My mentor retires to the seaside, and I leave her farewell party quieter than I arrived. I feel:
The exchange year ends, and the station goodbye makes for a mopey ride home. I feel:
My sister moves abroad for a wonderful job, and taping her boxes dampens me. I feel:
My roommate moves out to live with her partner, and the empty room leaves me melancholy. I feel:
My son leaves for campus tomorrow, and I pass his packed bags with a sinking feeling. I feel:
The summer staff say goodbye at season's end, and I lock up in a subdued mood. I feel:
My sister calls every week from her new city, and I still miss her at dinner. I feel:
My best friend texted just this morning, and the distance still gets to me tonight. I feel:
My son lives eight time zones away, and the quiet evenings get to me. I feel:
I pass the bakery where my friend and I met, and I miss our old Sundays. I feel:
My husband's posting has three months left, and the half-empty closet makes for a blue evening. I feel:
My college roommates are scattered across the map tonight, and I wish the map were smaller. I feel:
My grandmother's voice on our weekly call makes me miss her kitchen two countries away. I feel:
I write half a message to a faraway friend, and my mood dips as I type. I feel:
My childhood friend crosses my mind, and the long gap since our visit gets me down. I feel:
I miss the dog, who is only at my parents' house for the month. I feel:
A song from my teenage years comes on, and my mood turns wistful. I feel:
I look through the album of our shared summer, and a bittersweet feeling settles in. I feel:
The home videos show birthdays from long ago, and a mild melancholy comes with them. I feel:
My childhood street looks smaller now, and I idle at the corner shop too long. I feel:
The old ticket stubs fall from a book, and I sit with them for a while. I feel:
I find my old diary of big plans and put it back feeling quietly downhearted. I feel:
The toys in the attic bring back old afternoons, and I linger there, bittersweet. I feel:
My first apartment shows up in my photo feed, and the evening turns wistful. I feel:
The yearbook messages come from friends I rarely see, and reading them turns me wistful. I feel:
The old family car sold this spring, and its photo leaves me bittersweet tonight. I feel:
